title: No sea level equation
description: The simplest case: a Heaviside spherical cap at the pole, no ocean, no sea level equation. It coincides with Spada et al. (2011) test 1/2 for the cap load, and it establishes the level of disagreement between the codes before any ocean is added.

source.citation: Martinec, Z. et al. (2018). Geophysical Journal International 215(1), 389-414.

$outputs_comment: U is surface vertical displacement, N is geoid displacement, S is sea-surface variation, all along meridional cross-sections at the terminal time. h_UF is the thickness of the uniform water layer, ice_mass_grounded and ice_mass_floating are ice masses, and ocean_area is the ocean area as a fraction of 4 pi, all as functions of time. The list holds what the paper compares for this case.

profiles.profile: through the ice centre at the pole, longitude 0

comparison.$comment: Source: Martinec et al. (2018), section 5, figures 3 to 19. Difference intervals apply to the profiles at the terminal time. See docs/protocol/martinec2018.qmd, section Comparison method.

reference_data.reference: VEGA as the published difference files saw it, recovered as YS's profile minus YS's difference file on YS's 2048-point grid. resultsA_2026/Z_ZM_load.out is a second VEGA run, not the one behind figure 3; see correction benchmarkA-vega-supplied-run-differs.

reference_curves.$comment: How each reference curve in the group `reference` of the converted file is built. 'as shipped' copies VEGA (contributor ZM) from the archive. 'recovered' is YS's profile minus YS's own difference file, on YS's 2048-point grid: every difference file of the archive was computed against one finer VEGA profile, which the archive does not hold, and this gives it (docs/protocol/martinec2018.qmd, section How the reference is built).
